title: Is the adapter alive: soup adapters check and audit
description: soup adapters check says whether a LoRA adapter saved by the transformers path is trained; soup adapters audit compares a run's record with soup.yaml.

headings.title: What the record contains depends on the backend

blocks.html:
Is the adapter alive: soup adapters check and audit

Two commands added in v0.76.0 answer the question a healthy loss curve cannot: did this run produce an adapter that does anything, and did it train the way the config said? Both exist because each of the failures below looked like a normal run. v0.72.0 saved layer-streamed adapters under keys that loaded as the untuned base, a streamed run on peft 0.21 or newer saved an adapter holding zero tensors, and the MLX backend accepted training options it silently dropped (see what MLX honours).

CommandQuestionNeeds
soup adapters checkIs this LoRA adapter, saved by the transformers path, trained at all?the adapter directory only
soup adapters auditDid the run use the settings in soup.yaml?the adapter directory and the config

Neither loads a model, uses a GPU or touches the network. They are part of the soup adapters group described on the adapters page.

soup adapters check

blocks.code:
soup adapters check ./out/adapter
soup adapters check ./out/adapter --json

blocks.html: It reads adapter_model.safetensors and adapter_config.json and prints one verdict as its last line: alive, or inactive: <reason>.

blocks.code:
Adapter: /home/you/project/out/adapter
Total ||ΔW||_F: 13.316776
Live fraction: 100.0% (4/4 layers)
All-zero lora_B layers: 0/4
Leaked .inner. keys: 0
alive

blocks.html:
For every LoRA pair it computes ||ΔW||_F = scaling x ||B A||_F in float64, where scaling is lora_alpha / r (lora_alpha / sqrt(r) when the config sets use_rslora, and 1.0 when adapter_config.json has no r or lora_alpha). The total is the square root of the sum of the squares. A layer is live when its lora_B is not all zero and its delta is above zero.

The verdicts

The first match in this list wins, so a leaked-key adapter reports the leak even if its weights are also zero.

Last lineWhat it means
inactive: leaked .inner. keys detected (N tensors)Tensor names carry the extra .inner. segment that v0.72.0 layer streaming wrote. Loaded into an ordinary model they match nothing, and the result is the untuned base. The weights themselves can be healthy; the adapter is still reported inactive
inactive: incomplete LoRA pairs detected (N orphans)A lora_A without its lora_B, or the reverse
inactive: shape mismatch in LoRA projections (N layers)A pair whose shapes cannot multiply. Best effort: a pair that happens to fit the transposed layout is read as that layout and reported alive
inactive: non-finite weights detected (NaN/Inf)The printed total reads nan
inactive: no lora weights foundNo lora_A / lora_B tensors at all. This is the verdict for the zero-tensor adapter described on the v0.75.1 page, and for a non-LoRA PEFT adapter such as VeRA
inactive: all lora_B layers are zero (N/N)The adapter is still at its initial state: lora_B starts at zero, and nothing moved it
inactive: lora_B layers are zero (k/N)Any all-zero lora_B marks the whole adapter inactive, even when the other layers moved
inactive: total ||ΔW||_F is 0.0Every delta is zero by another route
aliveEvery pair is complete, finite and non-zero, and the total delta is above zero

soup adapters diff uses the same reader, so since v0.77.0 it reads bf16 adapters too.

Optional lines list the offending tensors for Zero lora_B projections:, Incomplete LoRA pairs:, Shape-mismatched LoRA pairs: and Leaked wrapper keys: (up to five, then ... and N more); Standalone non-LoRA tensors: N gives only a count. In the per-layer names an internal __LORA__ placeholder stands where lora_A or lora_B would be.

Exit codes

CodeMeaning
0alive
2inactive. A usage error (missing ADAPTER, unknown flag) is also 2, so read the last line as well as the code
1The command could not read the adapter (see below)

Exit 1 covers: a directory that is missing, outside the current directory or a symlink; no adapter_model.safetensors; an adapter_model.bin (re-save adapter as safetensors); a weights file over 2 GiB, which is refused from its size before it is opened; a corrupt weights file, or one holding a tensor in a dtype NumPy cannot hold here, such as FP8 (Unsupported safetensors weights in adapter_model.safetensors: tensor ... has unsupported dtype ...); an adapter_config.json that is not a JSON object; and, since v0.77.0, a missing NumPy (reported as an unreadable weights file, see below). Through v0.76.1 a missing safetensors package was on this list too.

What it cannot check

  • It needs NumPy. The command runs without PyTorch, and since v0.77.0 it reads the weights file's header itself, so the safetensors package is no longer needed (through v0.76.1 it was, and a core install exited 1 with safetensors package required; pip install safetensors). NumPy is not a dependency of the light core install, and without it the command exits 1 with Corrupt or unreadable safetensors weights in adapter_model.safetensors: No module named 'numpy': the file is fine, the package is missing. The training extras bring NumPy.
  • MLX adapters exit 1. The MLX trainer writes its weights as adapters.safetensors, and the command only looks for adapter_model.safetensors, so an MLX adapter directory reports no adapter_model.safetensors found. Use the audit command below for those: it reads the MLX record.
  • bfloat16 weights are read since v0.77.0 (#2058, #2063): they are widened to float32 exactly, so an adapter saved from a bf16 run is checked like any other. (Since closed in v0.77.0: through v0.76.1 a weights file holding bfloat16 tensors exited 1 with Corrupt or unreadable safetensors weights in adapter_model.safetensors: data type 'bfloat16' not understood, read by the v0.76.0 binary on a hand-built file.) The v0.77.0 behaviour was checked here on a hand-built file with two bf16 tensors (alive, exit 0; with lora_B all zero, inactive, exit 2), not on a trained adapter.
  • Only LoRA adapters saved by the transformers path are in scope. A VeRA adapter, or any other non-LoRA PEFT adapter, has no lora_A / lora_B pairs and reports inactive: no lora weights found, which is a statement about the format, not about whether it trained.
  • rank_pattern and alpha_pattern are ignored. An adapter with per-module ranks gets the single lora_alpha / r scaling, so the printed ||ΔW||_F is a health number, not an exact delta.
  • alive means the adapter moved away from its initial state. It says nothing about whether the model got better. For that, run soup ship.

--json

--json prints one object with sorted keys: adapter, verdict, verdict_line, reason, total_frobenius (null when not finite), live_fraction, live_layers, total_layers, all_zero_lora_b_layers, inner_keys, orphaned_layers, shape_mismatches, standalone_tensors and per_layer (per pair: name, frobenius, is_b_zero, has_non_finite, shape_a, shape_b). The exit code is the same as in text mode.

soup adapters audit

blocks.code:
soup adapters audit ./out/adapter --config soup.yaml
soup adapters audit ./out/adapter -c soup.yaml --json

blocks.html:
check asks whether the adapter is alive. audit asks whether the run that produced it used what you asked for. It loads soup.yaml through the schema (an omitted key is compared at its schema default), reads the settings recorded in adapter_config.json next to the weights, and compares them row by row.

The rows are optimizer, learning_rate (against the recorded peak, not the value copied from the config), scheduler, warmup_ratio, weight_decay, max_grad_norm, gradient_accumulation_steps, gradient_checkpointing, data.train_on_responses_only, lora.r and lora.alpha, plus nan_skip_fraction for task: grpo. Each ends as ok, DIVERGED or unknown. A setting the record cannot speak to is unknown and never ok.

The case it was written for is a warmup that rounds away. warmup_ratio: 0.03 over 12 optimizer updates is zero warmup steps, so training started at the peak learning rate:

blocks.code:
warmup_ratio: 0.03 x 12 optimizer updates rounds to 0, so training started at the peak learning rate; raise warmup_ratio or lower gradient_accumulation_steps to produce more updates

4 divergence(s)

blocks.html:
What the record contains depends on the backend

Adapter fromWhat adapter_config.json recordsWhat audit can check
The MLX backendThe effective optimizer, peak learning rate, schedule, warmup and total updates, weight decay, gradient clipping, accumulation, checkpointing, the response-only mask and the LoRA shapeAll eleven rows
The transformers backendPEFT's own file, which holds LoRA shape and nothing elseOnly lora.r and lora.alpha. The other nine rows read unknown, and the footer says so
Neither (an empty or unrecognised record)Nothing Soup can readEvery row is unknown

An MLX adapter trained with lora.use_rslora: true reads as diverged at v0.77.0. For r: 8 and alpha: 16 the lora.alpha row shows asked 16, ran 45.25483399593904, DIVERGED, and the command exits 2; the same config without use_rslora reads 16.0, ok. Checked here on an adapter_config.json written by Soup's own MLX record writer, not on a trained adapter. A CI step that gates on soup adapters audit fails such a run, so read the lora.alpha row before you act on the exit code.

An adapter that agrees on what it can check exits 0 with No divergences, 9 unchecked (or 11 unchecked for an empty record). That is a statement about what was checkable, not a clean bill for the run. A CI job should read checked_count in the --json output to tell "everything agreed" from "nothing could be compared".

Exit codes

CodeMeaning
0No row diverged. unknown rows do not fail the command
2At least one row is DIVERGED
1A path outside the working directory or a symlink, no adapter_config.json, a missing or invalid config, or a config the schema refuses (an unknown key exits 1 with Could not load <path>: unknown config key '<key>' - refused.). Since v0.76.1 that includes a config larger than 1 MiB or past the YAML nesting or expansion limits (Could not load big.yaml: Config file big.yaml is larger than 1048576 bytes; refusing)

A forgotten --config is exit 2 as well. --config is a required option, Click rejects the call before the command runs, and Click's code is 2, the same as a divergence. A script that treats 2 as "the run diverged" cannot tell the two apart from the code alone.

--json

The object holds record_kind (peft, mlx or unknown), diverged_count, unknown_count, checked_count, rows (per row: setting, asked, ran, status, detail) and unknown_reason. Warnings from loading the config go to stderr, so stdout parses.

  • Supply-chain security: scan, sign, verify and check-safetensors, which ask different questions (is it safe to load, is it the file that was signed).
  • Exit codes: both commands in the table, including the codes that collide with Click's.
